【图层准备】

前景图层（Z-index较高）： 一张城门插画（PNG/SVG格式），门洞区域为透明背景。

背景图层（Z-index较低）： 下一个需要展示的UI界面，被城门图层覆盖。

【交互与动画流程】

初始状态： 用户正常向下滚动页面，查看前面的内容。城门插画出现在下方。

触发点（Trigger）： 当用户滚动到城门的底部时，触发滚动锁定（Scroll Pinning / Position: sticky）。此时继续滑动鼠标滚轮或屏幕，页面整体不再向下滚动。

动画执行（Scrub）： 在锁定的状态下，用户的滚动进度直接映射为城门图层的 scale（放大）值。城门以门洞中心为缩放原点（Transform-origin: center）开始逐渐等比放大。

视觉穿透： 随着城门不断放大，透明的门洞区域逐渐占据整个屏幕，位于底层的“新UI界面”通过门洞完全显露出来，造成第一人称“走进城门”的视觉错觉。

结束状态： 当城门的边缘完全放大到屏幕视口之外（屏幕内只剩下新界面）时，解除滚动锁定。用户继续向下滑动，即可正常浏览新界面的内容。

Based on our review of academic research and existing heritage-related websites, we found that current heritage communication already provides useful foundations, but still lacks a playful, user-centred, and immersive way to help visitors understand Chang Gate.

Academic research shows that digital heritage should not only preserve information, but also connect virtual space with real historical sites, upgrade static explanation into immersive storytelling, and encourage users to become active participants instead of passive viewers. However, existing digital heritage projects often still focus on storing or displaying cultural materials, while weaker areas include narrative design, audience interaction, and recognizable cultural IP.

Research on contemporary heritage communication also emphasizes the importance of technology, emotional storytelling, and younger forms of expression, which supports our decision to design a more engaging web-based experience.

For Suzhou-related heritage, previous studies and existing products also gave us useful references. The Suzhou Ancient City Wall Projects show that restoration and planning around city walls, gates, riverside walking spaces, and scenic routes can successfully strengthen the historical atmosphere of the city. The study of Changmen Historical and Cultural Block also highlights the value of activating both physical elements, such as city walls, streets, and historical buildings, and intangible elements, such as traditional crafts and folk activities.

Commercial products such as the Suzhou Museum website, the Humble Administrator’s Garden VR tour, the Fengqiao Night Mooring introduction website, and Shantang Street VR/introduction pages show that many heritage platforms already contain rich historical information, image resources, virtual tours, and cultural background materials. 3 Things They Did Well

1. Strong heritage restoration and spatial planning
Existing projects, especially the Suzhou Ancient City Wall restoration work, show that physical heritage can be repaired and planned together with surrounding landscapes, walking routes, riverside spaces, and viewing points. This helps visitors feel the historical atmosphere of the city more directly.

2. Rich historical and cultural content
Some existing websites provide comprehensive background information. For example, the Fengqiao Night Mooring website includes history, poetry, cultural stories, maps, and local canal-related content. Suzhou Museum also organizes its collections into categories and provides digital collection displays.

3. Use of digital and visual presentation methods
Existing products already experiment with digital formats such as VR tours, panoramic viewing, 3D collection displays, and online heritage introductions. These methods make cultural sites more accessible beyond the physical visit and offer useful references for our own web-based design.

3 Things They Missed

1. The experience is often text-heavy and not interactive enough
Many heritage websites explain history through long blocks of text. This may be useful for professional or highly interested audiences, but for casual tourists it can feel difficult to read, especially during or after a short offline visit. The information exists, but users are not actively guided to explore it.

2. The storytelling lacks immersion and emotional engagement
Although some websites include historical background and cultural stories, the presentation often remains static. Users read about the past, but they do not feel like they are entering the historical scene or interacting with people, places, and events from that time. This makes it harder to build curiosity and memory.

3. There is a lack of playful, personalized, site-based exploration
Existing platforms usually present the same content to all visitors. They rarely adapt to different user types, such as casual photo-taking tourists, elderly visitors, or history enthusiasts. They also do not fully connect online interaction with the visitor’s real movement around the heritage site. # Role
You are an expert Frontend Creative Developer specializing in avant-garde UI/UX, Acid Graphics, Techno-Brutalism, and advanced GSAP animations. 

# Task
Create a responsive web component featuring 4 interactive cards introducing "Suzhou Changmen" (苏州阊门). The design must heavily utilize "Flat Acid Graphics" aesthetics combined with Cyber-glitch and sharp, Persona-style UI transitions. Each card will contain text and a continuously animating SVG object driven by GSAP, serving as a decorative background/corner element.

# Technical Stack
- HTML5 (Semantic and clean)
- CSS3 (Vanilla CSS, CSS Grid/Flexbox, Custom Properties for theming)
- JavaScript (GSAP core for all animations)
- SVG (Inline SVGs for all decorative objects)

# Design System & Aesthetics (Acid Graphics + Techno-Brutalism)
- Colors: Extremely high contrast. Dark background (e.g., #050505) with neon/acid accents (Acid Green, Hot Pink, Electric Blue, Neon Yellow, Silver/Grey).
- Typography: Brutalist. Bold, stretched, or highly tracking fonts for titles. Sharp, unrounded edges (border-radius: 0).
- Borders & Shadows: Thick, high-contrast solid borders. Hard drop shadows (no blur, e.g., `box-shadow: 8px 8px 0px #ff00ff`).
- Layout: Asymmetric or strictly grid-based. Include subtle marquee/ticker texts in the background of the cards.

# Content & Specific GSAP Animation Requirements
Generate 4 distinct cards. Each card must have a title, the provided description, and a dedicated `<svg>` decorative object animated with GSAP (`repeat: -1`).

**Card 1: 历史渊源 (Historical Origins)**
- Text: 作为苏州古城八大城门之一，阊门始建于春秋阖闾时期，见证了苏州两千五百多年的岁月变迁。
- Decorative Object: Concentric geometric rings or a wireframe Moebius strip.
- GSAP Animation: Infinite complex rotation on multiple axes (`rotationX`, `rotationY`, `rotationZ`) to create a 3D illusion of time shifting. Use `ease: "none"`.

**Card 2: 商业鼎盛 (Commercial Peak)**
- Text: 明清时期这里曾是全国水陆交通枢纽与顶级商业中心，历史上繁华程度被誉为“天下财富聚集之所”。
- Decorative Object: A wireframe ancient Chinese coin (square hole in a circle) or a brutalist diamond shape.
- GSAP Animation: Floating effect using `y` and infinite 3D flipping using `rotationY`. Combine with a slight `scale` pulse.

**Card 3: 文化地标 (Cultural Landmark)**
- Text: 古典名著《红楼梦》开篇便将阊门一带赞誉为“最是红尘中一二等富贵风流之地”，具有极高的文学与文化底蕴。
- Decorative Object: A liquid/fluid blob or a geometric flower.
- GSAP Animation: Liquid morphing effect. Animate the SVG path points or CSS `border-radius` values using GSAP to simulate a breathing, fluid, psychedelic distortion.

**Card 4: 建筑风貌 (Architectural Style)**
- Text: 它保留了江南水乡特有的水陆并行双城门格局，毗邻七里山塘，是探寻苏州传统水城风韵的绝佳起点。
- Decorative Object: Minimalist sharp arch lines (gate) with jagged wave patterns at the bottom.
- GSAP Animation: Implement a "Cyber-glitch" effect. Use GSAP timeline to create sudden, jagged `x` and `y` shifts, `skew` changes, and opacity flickers (`rough` ease if applicable) on the arch, while the wave lines pan infinitely horizontally.

# Constraints & Delivery Format
1. Output ONLY a single HTML file containing the HTML, `<style>` block, and `<script>` block. No markdown explanations outside the code block.
2. Include the CDN link for GSAP in the `<head>`.
3. Use inline SVG code for the animations, do not use external image links.
4. Add a "hover" interaction using GSAP for the cards (e.g., sharp scale-up, shadow offset change, or a torn-paper/diagonal reveal effect).
5. Ensure the text remains perfectly readable despite the chaotic/acid aesthetic of the background objects.

Reflection:
After spending a lot of time "vibecoding," I've realized that relying purely on it for frontend development still comes with significant struggles. Even though using workflows like Gemini or Cursor helps me get a project off the ground incredibly fast and build a structurally decent static interface, it often gives me false expectations about what the AI can actually do.
Once my requirements dive into complex micro-interactions or continuous transitions—like the city wall transition right before the historical timeline on my webpage—the AI gets trapped by the rigid framework it set up earlier. Since it lacks the ability to do a global refactor, it just forces patches onto the code, which makes the animations look stiff or completely ruins the effect.
Another major problem is that the AI only reads the code; it doesn't see the actual visual render. It often thinks a task is complete just by reading the syntax, but in reality, it leaves behind visual messes that are extremely hard to fix, like text overflows, messed-up Z-indexes, or broken responsive breakpoints.
As a result, since my frontend foundations are still developing, when I tackle complex interactive pages (like web apps with interactive maps or dynamic guides), I find myself forced to write incredibly dense prompts just to precisely control component lifecycles or the underlying CSS.
Furthermore, AI doesn't have the foresight to plan out an architecture as my ideas evolve. To implement a feature quickly, it often passes data across the wrong layers or hardcodes logic. Later on, when I try to add new requirements, a simple attempt to fix an overlapping component can end up destroying my entire global Flex layout.
Ultimately, AI does an incredible job of compressing the first 0 to 80% of the basic setup time, creating the illusion that "development is easy." But to push through that final 20% of highly stylized customization and fine-tuning, I've learned that I absolutely must have a solid technical foundation. Otherwise, I end up spending several times longer than I would have by just writing the code manually, all just to fill in the architectural and logical holes the AI dug for me.

【图层准备】

前景图层（Z-index较高）： 一张城门插画（PNG/SVG格式），门洞区域为透明背景。

背景图层（Z-index较低）： 下一个需要展示的UI界面，被城门图层覆盖。

【交互与动画流程】

初始状态： 用户正常向下滚动页面，查看前面的内容。城门插画出现在下方。

触发点（Trigger）： 当用户滚动到城门的底部时，触发滚动锁定（Scroll Pinning / Position: sticky）。此时继续滑动鼠标滚轮或屏幕，页面整体不再向下滚动。

动画执行（Scrub）： 在锁定的状态下，用户的滚动进度直接映射为城门图层的 scale（放大）值。城门以门洞中心为缩放原点（Transform-origin: center）开始逐渐等比放大。

视觉穿透： 随着城门不断放大，透明的门洞区域逐渐占据整个屏幕，位于底层的“新UI界面”通过门洞完全显露出来，造成第一人称“走进城门”的视觉错觉。

结束状态： 当城门的边缘完全放大到屏幕视口之外（屏幕内只剩下新界面）时，解除滚动锁定。用户继续向下滑动，即可正常浏览新界面的内容。
